title: Image in the high fibre-dimension locus recovers purity from an upper bound
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $d\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$. Suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Put
$$E=\{x\in X\mid\dim_x(X_{f(x)})\ge d\},$$
using topological dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be any morphism, and form $X'=X\times_T T'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to T'$. If $p(|X'|)\subseteq E$, then for every $x'\in X'$,
$$\dim_{x'}(X'_{f'(x')})=\dim_{p(x')}(X_{f(p(x'))})=d,$$
and every nonempty fibre of $f'$ is pure of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. In particular every irreducible component of such a fibre has dimension $d$. Empty source or fibres are allowed. No local finite presentation, flatness, separatedness, properness or finite type hypothesis on $g$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0EY2, lemma-descend-dimension-d, proof: final sentence recovering pure fibre dimension from the upper bound and image containment, including the component-generic-point argument.

proof.text: Fix $x\prime\in X\prime$, and write $x=p(x\prime)$, $t=f(x)$ and $t\prime=f\prime(x\prime)$. Finite type implies locally finite type, so lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change applies and gives $\dim_{x\prime}(X\prime_{t\prime})=\dim_x(X_t)$. Since $x\in E$, the right hand side is at least $d$. In the minimum defining $\dim_x(X_t)$, the whole fibre $X_t$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$, so $\dim_x(X_t)\le\dim X_t\le d$. Antisymmetry gives both displayed local dimensions equal to $d$. This holds for every $x\prime$.

source.place: Tag 0EY2, lemma-descend-dimension-d, final two sentences; expanded using morphisms.tex Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), part (1).

proof.text: Fix $t\prime\in T\prime$ and put $t=g(t\prime)$. By lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change the fibre $X\prime_{t\prime}$ is $Y_L$, where $Y=X_t$ and $L=\kappa(t\prime)$ is an extension of $k=\kappa(t)$. The structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type: by def-pc-scheme-fibre it is the base change of $f$, so apply lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change. Apply lem-trf-field-extension-component-local-dimension to this $Y$ and $L/k$. For each irreducible component $D$ of $Y_L$, that lemma supplies a generic point $z$ and the equality $\dim D=\dim_z(Y_L)$. The preceding step, applied to this point of $X\prime_{t\prime}$, makes the latter dimension $d$. Thus every component has dimension $d$, which is precisely pure dimension $d$ by def-weil-pure-dimension. If the fibre or source is empty there are no points or components to check. The invoked base-change statements allow arbitrary $g$ and arbitrary residue-field extension.

lean.statement: theorem fibre_purity_from_high_dimension_image {X T T' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (d : ℕ) (hupper : ∀ t : T, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber t) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (g : T' ⟶ T) (himage : Set.range (pullback.fst f g) ⊆ {x : X | (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber x)}) : (∀ x' : ↥(pullback f g), topologicalKrullDimAt ((pullback.snd f g).asFiber x') = topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber (pullback.fst f g x')) ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber (pullback.fst f g x')) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ t' : T', Nonempty ((pullback.snd f g).fiber t') → ((pullback.snd f g).fiber t').IsPureDimension d)
